521.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Maslama narrated to us, he said: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz delayed the prayer one day. Then ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr came in to him and informed him that al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba had delayed the prayer one day while he was in Iraq. Then Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī came in to him and said: What is this, Mughīra? Do you not know that Jibrīl ﷺ came down and prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he prayed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed; then he said: “I was commanded to do this”? Then ʿUmar said to ʿUrwa: Be mindful of what you relate! Was it Jibrīl himself who established the time of prayer for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? ʿUrwa said: Thus Bashīr ibn Abī Masʿūd used to relate from his father.
521.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The prayer times and their virtue.” ʿUrwa reports how Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī rebuked al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba for delaying the prayer, pointing out that Jibrīl came down and prayed and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed after him each time, five times. ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz then asks whether it was really Jibrīl who established the time of prayer; ʿUrwa refers to the report of Bashīr ibn Abī Masʿūd from his father.

522.matn: ʿUrwa said: And ʿĀʾisha told me: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the afternoon prayer while the sun was still in her room, before it became visible.”
522.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: ʿUrwa adds a report from ʿĀʾisha: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the afternoon prayer while the sun was still in her room, before it became visible.

523.matn: Qutayba ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, he said: ʿAbbād – that is, Ibn ʿAbbād – narrated to us, from Abū Jamra, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: “The delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: We belong to this clan of Rabīʿa, and we can reach you only in the sacred month. So command us with something that we may take from you and call to those who are behind us. He said: I command you with four things and forbid you four things: belief in Allah. Then he explained it to them: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving the zakāt, and that you pay me the fifth of what you take as spoils. And I forbid you the gourd (al-dubbāʾ), the ḥantam, the tarred vessel (al-muqayyar) and the hollowed trunk (al-naqīr).”
523.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The prayer times and their virtue.” Ibn ʿAbbās reports on the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays, who asked for instruction. The Prophet ﷺ commanded them four things – belief, prayer, zakāt and the fifth of the spoils – and forbade them four kinds of vessels.

524.matn: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Qays narrated to us, from Jarīr ibn ʿAbdallāh, he said: “I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to establish the prayer, to give the zakāt, and to be sincere toward every Muslim.”
524.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The prayer times and their virtue.” Jarīr ibn ʿAbdallāh reports that he pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to establish the prayer, to give the zakāt and to be sincere toward every Muslim.

525.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, he said: Shaqīq told me, he said: I heard Ḥudhayfa say: “We were sitting with ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: Which of you remembers the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the fitna (the trial)? I said: I do, just as he said it. He said: You are indeed bold in this – or about it. I said: The fitna of a man in his family, his property, his child and his neighbor is expiated by prayer, fasting, charity, commanding and forbidding. He said: That is not what I mean, but the fitna that surges as the sea surges. He said: You have nothing to fear from it, Commander of the Believers; between you and it is a closed door. He said: Will it be broken or opened? He said: It will be broken. He said: Then it will never be closed again. We said: Did ʿUmar know who the door is? He said: Yes, as surely as the night comes before the morrow; I told him a hadith that contains no errors. We were afraid to ask Ḥudhayfa, so we told Masrūq to ask him, and he said: The door is ʿUmar.”
525.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Prayer is an expiation.” Ḥudhayfa reports his conversation with ʿUmar about the fitna: the fitna of a man in his family, property, child and neighbor is expiated, among other things, by prayer; ʿUmar, however, meant the fitna that surges like the sea. Ḥudhayfa tells him that between him and it is a closed door that will be broken; when Masrūq asks him, he explains that the door is ʿUmar.

526.matn: Qutayba narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Sulaymān al-Taymī, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from Ibn Masʿūd: “A man had kissed a woman. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him. Then Allah revealed: ‘Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with evil deeds.’ The man said: O Messenger of Allah, is this for me? He said: For all of my community, all of them.”
526.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Prayer is an expiation.” Ibn Masʿūd reports about a man who had kissed a woman and told the Prophet ﷺ; the verse about prayer and good deeds was then revealed. When the man asked whether it applied to him, the Prophet answered that it applied to his whole community.

527.matn: Abū l-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us; al-Walīd ibn al-ʿAyzār said: He informed me, he said: I heard Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī say: The owner of this house narrated to us – and he pointed to the house of ʿAbdallāh –, he said: “I asked the Prophet ﷺ: Which deed is most beloved to Allah? He said: The prayer at its time. He said: Then which? He said: Then kindness to parents. He said: Then which? He said: Striving in the way of Allah.” He said: He told me these; had I asked him for more, he would have given me more.
527.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of prayer at its proper time.” ʿAbdallāh asks the Prophet ﷺ which deed is most beloved to Allah: the prayer at its time, then kindness to parents, then striving in the way of Allah. He adds that had he asked more, the Prophet would have told him more.

528.matn: Ibrāhīm ibn Ḥamza narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Ḥāzim and al-Darāwardī narrated to me, from Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Hurayra: He heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “What do you think: if there were a river at the door of one of you, in which he washed every day five times – would any of his dirt remain, what do you say? They said: None of his dirt would remain. He said: That is the likeness of the five prayers; Allah wipes out sins by them.”
528.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The five prayers are an expiation.” The Prophet ﷺ likens the five prayers to a river at one’s door in which one washes five times daily, leaving no dirt; in the same way Allah wipes out sins through the prayers.

529.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Mahdī narrated to us, from Ghaylān, from Anas, he said: “I recognize nothing of what existed in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. It was asked: Not even the prayer? He said: Have you not neglected in it what you have neglected?”
529.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Neglecting prayer beyond its time.” Anas says he recognizes nothing of what existed in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; asked about the prayer, he points out that people have neglected much in it.

530.matn: ʿAmr ibn Zurāra narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Wāṣil Abū ʿUbayda al-Ḥaddād informed us, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Rawwād, the brother of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, he said: I heard al-Zuhrī say: “I entered upon Anas ibn Mālik in Damascus while he was weeping. I said: What makes you weep? He said: I recognize nothing of what I knew except this prayer, and this prayer has been neglected.” And Bakr said: Muḥammad ibn Bakr al-Bursānī narrated to us: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Rawwād informed us, similarly.
530.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Neglecting prayer beyond its time.” Al-Zuhrī finds Anas weeping in Damascus; Anas says that of what he knew he recognizes only the prayer, and even that has been neglected. The addition “And Bakr said” gives a further line of transmission with similar wording.

531.matn: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “When one of you prays, he is conversing intimately with his Lord; so let him not spit to his right, but under his left foot.” And Saʿīd said, from Qatāda: Let him not spit in front of him or in front of his hands, but to the left or under his two feet. And Shuʿba said: Let him not spit in front of him or to his right, but to his left or under his foot. And Ḥumayd said, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ: Let him not spit in the direction of prayer or to his right, but to his left or under his foot.
531.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The one praying converses intimately with his Lord.” The Prophet ﷺ says that whoever prays is conversing intimately with his Lord and should therefore not spit to his right but under his left foot. The added statements “And Saʿīd said”, “And Shuʿba said” and “And Ḥumayd said” give variants without a full chain, naming the left, under the foot or – according to Ḥumayd – not in the direction of prayer.

532.matn: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Qatāda narrated to us, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Be moderate in prostration; let none of you stretch out his forearms like the dog. And if he spits, let him not spit in front of him or to his right, for he is conversing intimately with his Lord.”
532.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The one praying converses intimately with his Lord.” The Prophet ﷺ urges moderation in prostration, not stretching out the forearms like the dog, and not spitting forward or to the right, since the one praying converses intimately with his Lord.

533.matn: Ayyūb ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, he said: Abū Bakr narrated to us, from Sulaymān; Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān said: Al-Aʿraj – ʿAbd al-Raḥmān – and others narrated to us, from Abū Hurayra, and Nāfiʿ, the freedman of ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar: that both of them narrated to him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: “When the heat is intense, delay the prayer until it cools; for the intensity of the heat is from the blast of Jahannam.”
533.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Delaying the noon prayer until it cools in intense heat.” The Prophet ﷺ commands that, when the heat is intense, the prayer be delayed until it cools, and calls the intensity of the heat a blast of Jahannam. It is transmitted via Abū Hurayra and via Ibn ʿUmar.

535.matn: Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Ghundar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from al-Muhājir Abū l-Ḥasan, he heard Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abū Dharr, he said: “The caller to prayer of the Prophet ﷺ called the noon prayer. He said: Wait for the cool, wait for the cool! – or he said: Wait, wait! – And he said: The intensity of the heat is from the blast of Jahannam; when the heat is intense, delay the prayer until it cools. – Until we saw the shade of the hills.”
535.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Delaying the noon prayer until it cools in intense heat.” Abū Dharr reports that the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly told the caller to the noon prayer to wait for the cool – the narrator is unsure whether he said “Wait for the cool” or “Wait” – until the shade of the hills could be seen.

536.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: We memorized it from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “When the heat is intense, delay the prayer until it cools; for the intensity of the heat is from the blast of Jahannam,
536.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Delaying the noon prayer until it cools in intense heat.” The Prophet ﷺ commands delaying the prayer until it cools when the heat is intense. The text breaks off here in mid-sentence and is continued in the following hadith.

537.matn: and the Fire complained to its Lord and said: My Lord, parts of me have consumed other parts. So He permitted it two breaths: a breath in winter and a breath in summer. That is the most intense heat you feel and the most intense cold (zamharīr) you feel.”
537.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This hadith is, without a chain of its own, the continuation of the preceding one. The Prophet ﷺ reports that the Fire complained to its Lord and was permitted two breaths, one in winter and one in summer; they are the most intense heat and bitter cold that people feel.

538.matn: ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Al-Aʿmash narrated to us; Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Abū Saʿīd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Delay the noon prayer until it cools; for the intensity of the heat is from the blast of Jahannam.” Sufyān, Yaḥyā and Abū ʿAwāna followed him, from al-Aʿmash.
538.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Delaying the noon prayer until it cools in intense heat.” Abū Saʿīd relays the command of the Prophet ﷺ to delay the noon prayer until it cools. The addition “followed him …” names Sufyān, Yaḥyā and Abū ʿAwāna as further narrators from al-Aʿmash.

539.matn: Ādam ibn Abī Iyās narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: Muhājir Abū l-Ḥasan, a freedman of the Banū Taymallāh, narrated to us, he said: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī, he said: “We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and the caller wanted to call the noon prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said: Wait for the cool. Then he wanted to call, and he said to him: Wait for the cool. – Until we saw the shade of the hills. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: The intensity of the heat is from the blast of Jahannam; when the heat is intense, delay the prayer until it cools.” And Ibn ʿAbbās said: “Tatafayyaʾu” means “tatamayyalu” (they incline).
539.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Delaying the noon prayer until it cools while travelling.” Abū Dharr reports that on a journey the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly told the caller to wait before calling the noon prayer until the shade of the hills could be seen, and then described the intensity of the heat as a blast of Jahannam. The added sentence “And Ibn ʿAbbās said” is an explanation of a word without a chain.

540.matn: Abū l-Yamān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Anas ibn Mālik informed me: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out when the sun had passed the meridian, prayed the noon prayer, then stood on the pulpit and mentioned the Hour (al-Sāʿa); he mentioned that in it there are momentous things. Then he said: Whoever would like to ask about something, let him ask. You will not ask me about anything without my informing you, as long as I am in this place of mine. Then the people wept greatly, and he kept saying: Ask me! Then ʿAbdallāh ibn Ḥudhāfa al-Sahmī stood up and said: Who is my father? He said: Your father is Ḥudhāfa. Then he kept saying: Ask me! Then ʿUmar knelt on his knees and said: We are satisfied with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad as Prophet. Then he fell silent. Then he said: Just now Paradise and the Fire were shown to me, across the breadth of this wall, and I have seen nothing like the good and the evil.”
540.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the noon prayer is when the sun passes the meridian.” Anas reports that after the noon prayer, when the sun had passed the meridian, the Prophet ﷺ mentioned the Hour on the pulpit and invited questions. ʿAbdallāh ibn Ḥudhāfa asked about his father; ʿUmar pronounced the declaration of satisfaction with Allah, Islam and Muḥammad. The Prophet said that Paradise and the Fire had been shown to him.

541.matn: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abū l-Minhāl, from Abū Barza: “The Prophet ﷺ used to pray the dawn prayer while one of us could recognize the one sitting beside him, and he would recite in it between sixty and a hundred. He prayed the noon prayer when the sun had passed the meridian, and the afternoon prayer while one of us could go to the farthest part of Medina and return while the sun was still alive. And I have forgotten what he said about the sunset prayer. And he did not mind delaying the night prayer until a third of the night – then he said: until half the night.” And Muʿādh said: Shuʿba said: Then I met him once and he said: “or a third of the night.”
541.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the noon prayer is when the sun passes the meridian.” Abū Barza describes the prayer times of the Prophet ﷺ: the dawn prayer at a light in which one recognizes one’s neighbor; the noon prayer after the meridian; the afternoon prayer while the sun is still alive; the night prayer until a third or half of the night. The narrator says he forgot the statement about the sunset prayer; the addition “And Muʿādh said” gives a variant “or a third of the night.”

542.matn: Muḥammad, that is Ibn Muqātil, narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh informed us, he said: Khālid ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed us: Ghālib al-Qaṭṭān narrated to me, from Bakr ibn ʿAbdallāh al-Muzanī, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: “When we prayed the noon prayers behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we prostrated on our garments to protect ourselves from the heat.”
542.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the noon prayer is when the sun passes the meridian.” Anas reports that in the noon prayer behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ they prostrated on their garments to protect themselves from the heat.

543.matn: Abū l-Nuʿmān narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād – that is Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “The Prophet ﷺ prayed in Medina seven and eight: the noon and afternoon prayers, the sunset and night prayers.” Then Ayyūb said: Perhaps on a rainy night? He said: Perhaps.
543.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Delaying the noon prayer until the afternoon.” Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed “seven and eight” in Medina, namely noon and afternoon as well as sunset and night prayers. To Ayyūb’s question whether it was perhaps on a rainy night, Jābir ibn Zayd answers “Perhaps.”

544.matn: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, he said: Anas ibn ʿIyāḍ narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father: ʿĀʾisha said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the afternoon prayer while the sun had not yet left her room.”
544.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the afternoon prayer.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the afternoon prayer while the sun had not yet left her room.

545.matn: Qutayba narrated to us, he said: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the afternoon prayer while the sun was in her room and the shade had not yet appeared from her room.”
545.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the afternoon prayer.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the afternoon prayer while the sun was still in her room and the shade had not yet appeared.

546.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿUyayna informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “The Prophet ﷺ used to pray the afternoon prayer while the sun was shining in my room and the shade had not yet appeared.” And Mālik, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, Shuʿayb and Ibn Abī Ḥafṣa said: “and the sun, before it became visible.”
546.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the afternoon prayer.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed the afternoon prayer while the sun was shining in her room and the shade had not yet appeared. The addition “And Mālik … said” gives a differing wording (“and the sun, before it became visible”) without a full chain.

547.matn: Muḥammad ibn Muqātil narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh informed us, he said: ʿAwf informed us, from Sayyār ibn Salāma, he said: “I entered with my father upon Abū Barza al-Aslamī. My father said to him: How did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray the obligatory prayer? He said: He used to pray the noon prayer (al-hajīr), which you call the first, when the sun declined, and he prayed the afternoon prayer; after that one of us would return to his lodging at the farthest part of Medina while the sun was still alive. And I have forgotten what he said about the sunset prayer. He liked to delay the night prayer, which you call al-ʿatama, and he disliked sleeping before it and conversation after it. He would turn away from the dawn prayer when a man could recognize the one sitting beside him, and he would recite in it sixty to a hundred.”
547.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the afternoon prayer.” Abū Barza answers the question about the obligatory prayers of the Prophet ﷺ: noon prayer as the sun declines, the afternoon prayer while the sun is still alive, the night prayer rather late, no sleep before it and no conversation after it, the dawn prayer at a light in which one recognizes one’s neighbor. He says he forgot the statement about the sunset prayer.

548.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Maslama narrated to us, from Mālik, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: “We would pray the afternoon prayer, then a person would go out to the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf and find them praying the afternoon prayer.”
548.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the afternoon prayer.” Anas reports that after they prayed the afternoon prayer, one who went out to the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf would find them still praying the afternoon prayer.

549.matn: Ibn Muqātil narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh informed us, he said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿUthmān ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf informed us, he said: I heard Abū Umāma say: “We prayed the noon prayer with ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, then we went out until we entered upon Anas ibn Mālik and found him praying the afternoon prayer. I said: Uncle, what is this prayer you prayed? He said: The afternoon prayer, and this is the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that we used to pray with him.”
549.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the afternoon prayer.” Abū Umāma reports that after the noon prayer with ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz they went to Anas and found him praying the afternoon prayer; Anas explains that this was the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they prayed with him.

550.matn: Abū l-Yamān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Anas ibn Mālik narrated to me, he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the afternoon prayer while the sun was still high and alive; then the one who went would go to al-ʿAwālī and reach them while the sun was still high.” And some of al-ʿAwālī are four miles from Medina, or about that.
550.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the afternoon prayer.” Anas reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the afternoon prayer while the sun was still high and alive, and that afterwards one could go to al-ʿAwālī and find the sun still high there. The note on the distance of al-ʿAwālī (“four miles or about that”) is an explanatory remark at the end of the narration.

551.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: “We would pray the afternoon prayer; then the one who went from among us would go to Qubāʾ and reach them while the sun was still high.”
551.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the afternoon prayer.” Anas reports that they prayed the afternoon prayer and that one of them could then go to Qubāʾ while the sun was still high.

552.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if his family and his property had been plundered from him.”
552.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The sin of one who misses the afternoon prayer.” Ibn ʿUmar reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that for one who misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if his family and his property had been plundered from him.

553.matn: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated to us, from Abū Qilāba, from Abū l-Malīḥ, he said: “We were with Buraida on an expedition on a cloudy day. He said: Hasten to the afternoon prayer, for the Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever abandons the afternoon prayer, his deed has become void.”
553.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who abandons the afternoon prayer.” Abū l-Malīḥ reports that Buraida, on an expedition on a cloudy day, urged them to hasten to the afternoon prayer and gave as the reason the Prophet’s ﷺ statement that the deed of one who abandons the afternoon prayer has become void.

554.matn: Al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us, he said: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiya narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Qays, from Jarīr, he said: “We were with the Prophet ﷺ. He looked at the moon one night, meaning the full moon, and said: You will see your Lord as you see this moon; you will not be crowded in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so. Then he recited: ‘And glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before the setting.’” Ismāʿīl said: “Do so; let them not escape you.”
554.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of the afternoon prayer.” Jarīr reports that the Prophet ﷺ said on a full-moon night that the Lord will be seen as the moon is seen, and urged them not to miss the prayer before sunrise and before sunset; he recited a Qurʾān verse in this connection. The closing words are from Ismāʿīl, a narrator in the chain.

555.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to us, from Abū l-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Angels of the night and angels of the day succeed one another among you, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend, and He asks them, though He knows them best: How did you leave My servants? They say: We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.”
555.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of the afternoon prayer.” Abū Hurayra reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that angels of the night and angels of the day succeed one another, gather at the dawn and afternoon prayers, and then, when asked by Allah, testify that they left the servants praying and found them praying.

556.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If one of you catches one prostration of the afternoon prayer before the sun sets, let him complete his prayer; and if he catches one prostration of the dawn prayer before the sun rises, let him complete his prayer.”
556.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who catches a rakʿa of the afternoon prayer before sunset.” Abū Hurayra reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: whoever catches one prostration of the afternoon prayer before sunset, or one prostration of the dawn prayer before sunrise, should complete that prayer.

557.matn: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim ibn ʿAbdallāh, from his father, that he informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Your stay compared with the nations that passed before you is only like the time between the afternoon prayer and the setting of the sun. The people of the Torah were given the Torah; they worked until midday, then they grew weak, and they were given one qīrāṭ each. Then the people of the Gospel were given the Gospel; they worked until the afternoon prayer, then they grew weak, and they were given one qīrāṭ each. Then we were given the Qurʾān, and we worked until the setting of the sun, and we were given two qīrāṭs each. The people of the two Books said: Our Lord, You gave these two qīrāṭs each and gave us one qīrāṭ each, though we did more work? He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Have I wronged you in any of your wage? They said: No. He said: That is My bounty; I give it to whom I will.”
557.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who catches a rakʿa of the afternoon prayer before sunset.” Ibn ʿUmar reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a parable: the Muslims’ stay compared with earlier nations is like the time between the afternoon prayer and sunset. The people of the Torah and the Gospel received one qīrāṭ each, the Muslims two each; to the complaint of the two groups Allah replies that He withheld nothing of the wage and that the extra is His bounty.

558.matn: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abū Burda, from Abū Mūsā, from the Prophet ﷺ: “The parable of the Muslims, the Jews and the Christians is like that of a man who hired people to work for him until night. They worked until midday, then they said: We have no need of your wage. So he hired others and said: Complete the rest of your day, and you will have what I stipulated. They worked until the time of the afternoon prayer came; then they said: What we have worked is yours. Then he hired other people; they worked the rest of their day until the sun disappeared, and they received the full wage of the two groups.”
558.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who catches a rakʿa of the afternoon prayer before sunset.” Abū Mūsā reports from the Prophet ﷺ a parable of Muslims, Jews and Christians with a man who hires workers: the first stop at midday, the second at the time of the afternoon prayer, and the last work until sunset and receive the full wage of both groups.

559.matn: Muḥammad ibn Mihrān narrated to us, he said: Al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, he said: Abū l-Najāshī [that is ʿAṭāʾ ibn] Ṣuhayb, the freedman of Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj, narrated to us, he said: I heard Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj say: “We used to pray the sunset prayer with the Prophet ﷺ; then one of us would leave, and he could still see the places where his arrows fell.”
559.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the sunset prayer.” Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj reports that they prayed the sunset prayer with the Prophet ﷺ and that one of them could then leave and still see where his arrows fell. The note in square brackets on Abū l-Najāshī is an explanation within the transmitted text.

560.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Saʿd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, he said: “Al-Ḥajjāj arrived, and we asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh. He said: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray the noon prayer at the midday heat, the afternoon prayer while the sun was clear, the sunset prayer when it had set, and the night prayer sometimes this way and sometimes that: when he saw that they had gathered he hastened, and when he saw that they were slow he delayed it. And the dawn prayer – they used to pray it, or the Prophet ﷺ used to pray it – in the darkness before daybreak.”
560.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the sunset prayer.” Asked about it, Jābir gives the prayer times of the Prophet ﷺ: noon prayer at the midday heat, afternoon prayer while the sun is clear, sunset prayer after it has set, night prayer earlier or later depending on whether the people had gathered, dawn prayer in the darkness. The narrator is unsure whether he said “they” or “the Prophet ﷺ”.

561.matn: Al-Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Abī ʿUbayd narrated to us, from Salama, he said: “We used to pray the sunset prayer with the Prophet ﷺ when it had disappeared behind the veil.”
561.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the sunset prayer.” Salama reports that they prayed the sunset prayer with the Prophet ﷺ when the sun had disappeared behind the veil.

562.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, he said: I heard Jābir ibn Zayd from Ibn ʿAbbās: “The Prophet ﷺ prayed seven together and eight together.”
562.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the sunset prayer.” Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet ﷺ prayed “seven together and eight together.” The wording gives only the numbers; scholars usually relate them to combining the sunset and night prayers (seven rakʿas) and the noon and afternoon prayers (eight rakʿas). That is an interpretation, not wording of the hadith.

563.matn: Abū Maʿmar, that is ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr, narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, from al-Ḥusayn, he said: ʿAbdallāh ibn Buraida narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh al-Muzanī narrated to me that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not let the Bedouins overcome you in the name of your prayer, the sunset prayer.” He said: “The Bedouins,” and they say: “It is ʿishāʾ.”
563.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who disliked calling the sunset prayer ‘ʿishāʾ’.” ʿAbdallāh al-Muzanī reports that the Prophet ﷺ warned against letting the Bedouins, who call it “ʿishāʾ,” take away the name of the sunset prayer.

564.matn: ʿAbdān narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh informed us, he said: Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī; Sālim said: ʿAbdallāh narrated to me, he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us one night in the ʿishāʾ prayer, which is the one people call al-ʿatama; then he turned away, came toward us and said: Do you see this night of yours? A hundred years from it, none of those who are on the back of the earth will remain.”
564.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The names ‘ʿishāʾ’ and ‘ʿatama’ and one who considered both acceptable.” ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in the night prayer that people call “al-ʿatama” and afterwards addressed them with a statement about a hundred years.

565.matn: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, that is Ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, he said: “We asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh about the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: He used to pray the noon prayer at the midday heat, the afternoon prayer while the sun was alive, the sunset prayer when it had set, and the night prayer: when the people were many he hastened, and when they were few he delayed it; and the dawn prayer in the darkness.”
565.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the night prayer when people gather or are late.” Jābir gives the prayer times of the Prophet ﷺ: noon prayer at the midday heat, afternoon prayer while the sun is alive, sunset prayer after it has set, night prayer earlier when many were present and later when few, dawn prayer in the darkness.

566.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: Al-Layth narrated to us, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa: ʿĀʾisha informed him, she said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the night prayer one night, and that was before Islam had spread. He did not come out until ʿUmar said: The women and children have slept. Then he came out and said to the people of the mosque: None of the people of the earth is waiting for it except you.”
566.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of the night prayer.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the night prayer one night, before Islam had spread, and came out only after ʿUmar pointed out that the women and children had gone to sleep; he then told the people in the mosque that no one else on earth was waiting for this prayer.

567.matn: Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma informed us, from Burayd, from Abū Burda, from Abū Mūsā, he said: “I and my companions who had come with me on the ship were staying at Baqīʿ Buṭḥān, while the Prophet ﷺ was in Medina. A group of them would take turns attending the Prophet ﷺ at the night prayer each night. Then we, I and my companions, met the Prophet – peace be upon him – and he had some business in one of his affairs. So he delayed the prayer until the night was well advanced. Then the Prophet ﷺ came out and prayed with them. When he had finished his prayer, he said to those present: Take it easy, rejoice! It is part of Allah’s favor upon you that none of the people prays at this hour except you. – Or he said: None has prayed at this hour except you. – The narrator does not know which of the two phrases he said. Abū Mūsā said: So we returned, rejoicing at what we had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
567.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of the night prayer.” Abū Mūsā reports that the Prophet ﷺ once delayed the night prayer far into the night because of some business, then prayed with those present and announced to them, as a favor from Allah, that no one else prayed at that hour. The narrator is unsure of the exact phrase.

568.matn: Muḥammad ibn Salām narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī informed us, he said: Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ narrated to us, from Abū l-Minhāl, from Abū Barza: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ “disliked sleeping before the night prayer and conversation after it.”
568.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “What is disliked of sleeping before the night prayer.” Abū Barza reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked sleeping before the night prayer and conversation after it.

569.matn: Ayyūb ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, he said: Abū Bakr narrated to me, from Sulaymān; he said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān: Ibn Shihāb informed me, from ʿUrwa: ʿĀʾisha said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the night prayer until ʿUmar called out to him: The prayer! The women and children have slept. Then he came out and said: None of the people of the earth is waiting for it except you.” He said: “On that day prayer was offered only in Medina, and they used to pray in the time between the disappearance of the twilight glow and the first third of the night.”
569.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Sleeping before the night prayer for one overcome by it.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the night prayer until ʿUmar pointed out that the women and children had slept, and that he then said no one else on earth was waiting for it. The closing sentence gives the time of the night prayer as between the disappearance of the twilight glow and the first third of the night.

570.matn: Maḥmūd narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed me, he said: Nāfiʿ informed me, he said: ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was kept from it one night and delayed it until we had fallen asleep in the mosque, then we woke, then we slept, then we woke. Then the Prophet ﷺ came out to us and said: None of the people of the earth is waiting for the prayer except you.” And Ibn ʿUmar did not mind whether he prayed it early or delayed it, as long as he did not fear that sleep would overcome him past its time, and he used to sleep before it. Ibn Jurayj said: I said to ʿAṭāʾ.
570.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Sleeping before the night prayer for one overcome by it.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the night prayer one night until the people in the mosque had fallen asleep, and then told them that no one else on earth was waiting for it. The addition about Ibn ʿUmar’s own practice is his statement, not wording of the Prophet ﷺ. The sentence “Ibn Jurayj said: I said to ʿAṭāʾ” breaks off; its continuation is in the next passage.

571.matn: And he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the night prayer one night until the people slept and woke, slept and woke. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb stood up and said: The prayer! ʿAṭāʾ said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out – it is as if I see him now – his head dripping water, with his hand placed on his head, and he said: Were it not that I would burden my community, I would order them to pray it like this. I asked ʿAṭāʾ to confirm how the Prophet ﷺ had placed his hand on his head, as Ibn ʿAbbās had told him. So ʿAṭāʾ spread his fingers apart a little for me, then placed the tips of his fingers on the side of the head, then joined them and passed them over the head like that until his thumb touched the edge of the ear that is toward the face, at the temple and the side of the beard; he neither fell short nor gripped, except like that. And he said: Were it not that I would burden my community, I would order them to pray like this.”
571.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Sleeping before the night prayer for one overcome by it.” This passage continues the previous one: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet ﷺ delayed the night prayer until the people had slept and woken repeatedly, until ʿUmar urged the prayer, and that he came out with his head wet and said he would order them to pray it like this were it not a burden on his community. The description of the hand position is from ʿAṭāʾ.

572.matn: ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Muḥāribī narrated to us, he said: Zāʾida narrated to us, from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, from Anas, he said: “The Prophet ﷺ delayed the night prayer until the middle of the night, then he prayed, then he said: The people have prayed and gone to sleep. But you are in prayer as long as you are waiting for it.”
572.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the night prayer until midnight.” Anas reports that the Prophet ﷺ delayed the night prayer until the middle of the night, then prayed and said that the people had prayed and slept, while those waiting are in prayer as long as they wait.

573.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl; Qays narrated to us: Jarīr ibn ʿAbdallāh said to me: “We were with the Prophet ﷺ when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: You will see your Lord as you see this; you will not be crowded in seeing Him – lā tuḍāmmūna or lā tuḍāhūna. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so. Then he said: ‘So glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.’”
573.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of the dawn prayer.” Jarīr reports that the Prophet ﷺ said on a full-moon night that the Lord will be seen as the moon is seen, and urged them not to miss the prayer before sunrise and before sunset; he cited a Qurʾān verse. The narrator is unsure whether he said “lā tuḍāmmūna” or “lā tuḍāhūna.”

574.matn: Hudba ibn Khālid narrated to us, he said: Hammām narrated to us: Abū Jamra narrated to me, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Mūsā, from his father: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever prays the two cool prayers will enter Paradise.” And Ibn Rajāʾ said: Hammām narrated to us, from Abū Jamra: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Qays informed him of this.
574.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of the dawn prayer.” Abū Mūsā reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that whoever prays “the two cool prayers” will enter Paradise; these are usually understood to be the dawn and the afternoon prayers. The addition after “And Ibn Rajāʾ said” gives a further line of transmission for the same hadith.

575.matn: ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: Hammām narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas: Zayd ibn Thābit told him: “They ate the pre-dawn meal (suḥūr) with the Prophet ﷺ, then they stood up for the prayer. I said: How much was between the two? He said: About fifty or sixty, meaning verses.” (ḥ – the chain of transmission changes here)
575.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the dawn prayer.” Zayd ibn Thābit reports that they ate the pre-dawn meal with the Prophet ﷺ and then stood up for the prayer; the interval was about fifty or sixty verses. The sign “ḥ” at the end marks a switch to another chain of transmission.

576.matn: Ḥasan ibn Ṣabbāḥ narrated to us, he heard Rawḥ: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas ibn Mālik: “The Prophet of Allah ﷺ and Zayd ibn Thābit ate the pre-dawn meal. When they had finished it, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood up for the prayer and prayed. We said to Anas: How much was between their finishing the meal and their entering the prayer? He said: As much as a man recites fifty verses.”
576.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the dawn prayer.” Anas reports that the Prophet ﷺ and Zayd ibn Thābit ate the pre-dawn meal and that the Prophet ﷺ then stood up for the prayer; the interval was the time in which a man recites fifty verses.

577.matn: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways narrated to us, from his brother, from Sulaymān, from Abū Ḥāzim, that he heard Sahl ibn Saʿd say: “I would eat the pre-dawn meal with my family; then I would hurry to catch the dawn prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
577.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the dawn prayer.” Sahl ibn Saʿd reports that he ate the pre-dawn meal with his family and then hurried to catch the dawn prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

578.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: Al-Layth informed us, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ʿĀʾisha informed him, she said: “The believing women used to attend the dawn prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, wrapped in their cloaks; then they would return to their homes when they had finished the prayer, and no one recognized them because of the darkness.”
578.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The time of the dawn prayer.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the believing women, wrapped in their cloaks, attended the dawn prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and then returned to their homes without being recognized because of the darkness.

579.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Maslama narrated to us, from Mālik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, and from Busr ibn Saʿīd, and from al-Aʿraj; they relate it from Abū Hurayra: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever catches one rakʿa of the dawn prayer before the sun rises has caught the dawn prayer. And whoever catches one rakʿa of the afternoon prayer before the sun sets has caught the afternoon prayer.”
579.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who catches a rakʿa of the dawn prayer.” Abū Hurayra reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: whoever catches one rakʿa of the dawn prayer before sunrise has caught the dawn prayer, and whoever catches one rakʿa of the afternoon prayer before sunset has caught the afternoon prayer. The report runs through three narrators who relate from Abū Hurayra.

580.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Hurayra: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever catches one rakʿa of the prayer has caught the prayer.”
580.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who catches a rakʿa of the prayer.” Abū Hurayra reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: whoever catches one rakʿa of the prayer has caught the prayer.

581.matn: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Abū l-ʿĀliya, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: “Men with whom one is satisfied testified to me, and the one with whom I am most satisfied is ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ forbade prayer after the dawn prayer until the sun rises, and after the afternoon prayer until it sets.” Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Qatāda: I heard Abū l-ʿĀliya from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: “People told me this.”
581.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying after the dawn prayer until the sun rises high.” Ibn ʿAbbās reports that esteemed men, among them ʿUmar, testified to him that the Prophet ﷺ forbade prayer after the dawn prayer until sunrise and after the afternoon prayer until sunset. A second chain runs through Shuʿba to Abū l-ʿĀliya and Ibn ʿAbbās with the wording “People told me this.”

582.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Hishām, he said: My father informed me, he said: Ibn ʿUmar informed me, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not deliberately seek the rising of the sun or its setting with your prayers.”
582.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying after the dawn prayer until the sun rises high.” Ibn ʿUmar reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that one should not deliberately time one’s prayers for sunrise or sunset.

583.matn: And he said: Ibn ʿUmar narrated to me, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the rim of the sun rises, delay the prayer until it has risen; and when the rim of the sun disappears, delay the prayer until it has fully disappeared.” ʿAbda followed him in this narration.
583.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying after the dawn prayer until the sun rises high.” Ibn ʿUmar reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that one should delay prayer while the rim of the sun appears at sunrise, until it has risen, and at sunset, until it has fully disappeared. The closing sentence names ʿAbda as a further narrator of the same statement.

584.matn: ʿUbayd ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Abū Usāma, from ʿUbaydallāh, from Khubayb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿĀṣim, from Abū Hurayra: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ “forbade two kinds of sales, two kinds of garments and two prayers: He forbade prayer after daybreak until the sun rises, and after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets; and wrapping oneself up completely (ishtimāl al-ṣammāʾ) and squatting in a single garment, exposing one’s private parts to the sky; and sale by throwing (munābadha) and by touching (mulāmasa).”
584.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying after the dawn prayer until the sun rises high.” Abū Hurayra reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two kinds of sales, two kinds of garments and two prayers; as the prayer prohibitions he names prayer after daybreak until sunrise and after the afternoon prayer until sunset.

585.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you should aim to pray at the rising of the sun or at its setting.”
585.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying after the dawn prayer until the sun rises high.” Ibn ʿUmar reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that none of them should aim to pray at sunrise or sunset.
